covers: Weekend and Monday to 12:15 SAST: Moody's on SA's budget update, Middle East oil news, neocloud selloff, Brazil's election, Pick n Pay results, US futures, rand and the week ahead
headline: Moody's calls South Africa's budget update credit positive (no rating action); oil eases about 2% and US futures rise ahead of a Fed week
summary: Moody's said on Monday that the medium-term budget statement is positive for South Africa's credit profile and that debt has probably peaked, but took no rating action on its Ba2 rating with a positive outlook; the rand was near R16.61/$ (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 26 Oct). US stock futures rose on Sunday evening, S&P 500 +0.3% and Nasdaq-100 +0.4%, while neocloud stocks CoreWeave and Nebius fell about 3% before the open after Elon Musk warned that many such firms face 'guppy-level death' (CNBC, 25 Oct; Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct). Brent fell 2.1% to $114.3 and gold hovered around $4,000 near a three-month low (HDFC Sky; FinanceFeeds, 26 Oct); lower oil eases some pressure on SA fuel prices, but supply risk is still high.

items.title: Moody's says South Africa's budget update is credit positive; no rating action
items.summary: In a report on Monday, Moody's said the medium-term budget policy statement is positive for South Africa's credit profile, citing continued fiscal consolidation despite higher oil prices. The FY2026 consolidated deficit target was cut to 3.9% of GDP from 4.0%, helped by a R17.1bn upward revision to tax revenue. Moody's sees government debt at 84.9% of GDP by FY2028, down from about 86.8% in FY2025, and says debt has 'probably peaked', though interest took 18.8% of revenue in FY2025. It also called the draft fiscal-rules law credit positive. South Africa stays at Ba2 with a positive outlook; Moody's did not announce a rating action (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 26 Oct).

items.title: Oil falls about 2% despite weekend Houthi attack claims on Saudi oil sites
items.summary: On Monday morning Brent was at $114.3 a barrel (−2.1%) and WTI at $101 (−2.2%), easing from near six-month highs. The Houthis said they attacked a Saudi airport and oil facilities over the weekend, and Saudi Arabia said it intercepted more missiles and drones on Sunday. The US also approved a 400,000-barrel release from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve after a Louisiana refinery disruption (HDFC Sky, 26 Oct). Reported targets were an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery and the East-West pipeline; damage has not been confirmed (Babypips, 26 Oct).

items.title: Futures rise after the S&P 500's second losing week
items.summary: On Sunday evening S&P 500 futures were up 0.3%, Dow futures up 85 points (0.2%) and Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.4%. On Friday the Dow fell more than 650 points, the S&P 500 lost 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.2% (CNBC, 25 Oct).

items.title: Neocloud stocks slip before the open after Musk's 'guppy-level death' warning
items.summary: In pre-market trading on Monday, CoreWeave was down 2.7% and Nebius down 3.5% after Elon Musk posted that 200+ 'neocloud' data-centre firms face 'guppy-level death and consolidation' because lenders are reluctant to fund them. CoreWeave's bonds were also sold. BofA's Tal Liani called the CoreWeave selloff sentiment-driven and kept his $140 target (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct).

items.title: Busy week: Fed decision Wednesday, big tech results, GDP and PCE Thursday
items.summary: The Fed announces its decision on Wed 28 Oct at 18:00 GMT (20:00 SAST) and is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00%. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close on Wednesday, Amazon and Intel on Thursday. Q3 GDP (forecast 3.1% annualised) and core PCE (forecast +0.2% m/m) come out on Thursday, and the ECB (Thursday) and Bank of Japan (Friday) also decide on rates (Babypips, 26 Oct). Futures pricing (CME FedWatch) gives a 75% chance of a Fed hike in December (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct).

items.title: Musk says SpaceX closed a $40 billion debt deal for AI chips
items.summary: In a Sunday post on X, Elon Musk said SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt financing, mainly for GPUs arriving in the first half of 2027. He warned that lenders have nearly stopped funding 'neocloud' data-centre firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius. The claim comes from Musk's post; no filing or lender statement has been cited (Yahoo Finance, 25 Oct).

items.title: Pick n Pay narrows its half-year loss as Boxer keeps growing
items.summary: For the six months to end-August, group turnover rose 2.4% to R60.5bn, with Boxer up 6.3%, the core Pick n Pay segment mostly flat and online sales up 35.4%. The headline loss narrowed to R299m from R439m a year earlier (40.71c a share from 59.77c), and group trading profit rose 58.1% to R490m (BusinessDay, 26 Oct). Pick n Pay is not a covered company.

items.title: Rand steady at about R16.61/$ ahead of the Fed and month-end data
items.summary: At 06:02 GMT the rand was at 16.6125 to the dollar, little changed from its previous close, and the 2035 bond yield was steady at 8.635% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct).

items.title: Stats SA to publish rebased GDP figures on Thursday
items.summary: This week Stats SA releases rebased and benchmarked GDP estimates and the September PPI on Thu 29 Oct; Nedbank expects PPI inflation to rise to 5.3% from 5.0%. SARS trade data for September follows on Friday, after August's R20.5bn surplus (Business Day, 26 Oct).

items.title: Emerging markets: Lula wins Brazil's presidential run-off
items.summary: Incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Flávio Bolsonaro in a tight run-off on Sunday 25 October (Al Jazeera, 25–26 Oct). Brazil is a large emerging market alongside South Africa, so the result and any challenge to it can sway emerging-market sentiment and the rand this week. Final vote shares were not confirmed in the sources we could open.

items.title: Gold hovers around $4,000 near a three-month low
items.summary: Spot gold was at $4,009.87 (+0.4%) at 03:42 GMT as oil eased, after Friday's first close below $4,000 since mid-July and a roughly 4% weekly fall, the steepest since June (FinanceFeeds, 26 Oct). Later on Monday morning it was quoted at $3,987.45 (−0.2%) (NewsBytes, 26 Oct).

items.title: NVIDIA: SpaceX says it has funding for a large AI-chip order
items.summary: Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion in debt for GPUs (Yahoo Finance, 25 Oct). Earlier October reports said the money was for NVIDIA chips, but this has not been confirmed. If confirmed, it supports demand for NVIDIA (BUY on our list, LRC target $262.56). The other side: neocloud customers CoreWeave and Nebius fell about 3% before Monday's open after Musk warned lenders are pulling back from such firms (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct), a demand risk to watch. Rating unchanged.
